facts.text: Midtown Phillips takes its name from Wendell Phillips, the Boston abolitionist honored here despite the neighborhood’s origins on former Dakota land.
The former Sears, Roebuck building on Lake Street now houses Midtown Global Market, a food hub that reflects the area’s cultural mix.
The $189 million Midtown Exchange project transformed the vacant Sears site into a mixed‑use complex of offices, hotel, retail and housing.
Stewart Park and Andersen United School sit in Midtown Phillips’ heart, serving as green space and educational hub for residents.
Chicago Avenue, the neighborhood’s western edge, was declared a wellness corridor to promote healthy living across Midtown Phillips.
Midtown and East Phillips Neighborhood Association merged into a single group, uniting volunteers to advocate for a vibrant, safe community.
